title: Frontend maintenance mode gate with full-page downtime screen

requirements.summary: Add a frontend-configurable maintenance mode that replaces the entire app UI with a full-page maintenance message.
acceptanceCriteria: A new environment variable is documented in frontend/.env.example (e.g., VITE_MAINTENANCE_MODE) with guidance on accepted values.
When maintenance mode is enabled, the app renders a maintenance screen and does not render the normal application content (HeroSection/MainContent) or show authentication actions.
The maintenance screen user-facing text is in English and clearly indicates the app is temporarily unavailable.
When maintenance mode is disabled/unset, the app behaves exactly as it did before the change.

file_operations.description: Document a new Vite env var (VITE_MAINTENANCE_MODE) that controls maintenance mode, including accepted values (e.g., true/1/on/yes to enable; false/0/off/no or unset to disable) and a brief note that it is evaluated at build/runtime per Vite env behavior.

Add a small env parsing helper (e.g., reading import.meta.env.VITE_MAINTENANCE_MODE and normalizing common truthy/falsey strings) and export a boolean flag used by the app to decide whether to show the maintenance screen.
Create a full-page MaintenanceScreen component (English copy) that clearly states the app is temporarily unavailable; ensure it is self-contained and does not include header/footer/auth controls.

Wire maintenance mode into the root UI: read the maintenance flag and, when enabled, render only the MaintenanceScreen (no AppShell/Header/Footer/HeroSection/MainContent/ProfileSetupDialog/Toaster). Refactor to avoid calling authentication/profile hooks in maintenance mode by moving normal app rendering into a separate component that is only mounted when maintenance mode is disabled.
